parties:
Md. Ismail @ Haji Md. Ismail
Vs.
The State and another
full_judgment:
Siddiqur Rahman Miah, J: This Rule on an application filed under section 561 A of the Code of criminal Procedure was issued upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the proceedings in Sessions Case No.1062 of 2006 arising out of CR Case No. 183 of 2006 (Doublemooring Zone) under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 now pending in the court of the learned Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge, 1st Court, Chittagong should not be quashed. 

 2. Necessary facts for the purpose of disposal of this Rule is that on 25.06.2006 the petitioner as complainant filed the petition of complaint before the court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong being CR Case No.183 of 2006 (Doublemooring Zone) alleging inter alia that there was a regular business transaction between the accused petitioner and the complainant opposite party; that on 22.11.2005 and 23.11.2005 the accused petitioner paid 3 (three) postdated cheques to the complainant amounting to Taka 13,81.700/= only in his office out of their business transaction; that the cheques deposited in the United Commercial Bank but the said cheques has been dishonoured due to insufficient fund on 18.05.2006 and that thereafter on 23.05.2006 legal notice has been issued on behalf of the complainant to the accused petitioner but the said notice returned with report that the notice receiver has not been available and till today there is no reply. Hence the complainant filed the petition of complaint before the court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong. 

 5. On 08.10.2006 the case record was transmitted to the court of Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Chittagong which was registered as Sessions Case No.1062 of 2006. The learned Sessions Judge took cognizance under section 138 of the Negotiable Instrument Act against the petitioner and fixed for appearance of the accused petitioner on 13.11.2006. 

 7. On 04.11.2006 the case was fixed for hearing. The prayer for adjournment was allowed and on 03.1.2008 was fixed for further hearing. 

 8. Thereafter the accused petitioner being aggrieved filed a Miscellaneous Case before this court under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure against the initiation of proceedings of Sessions Case No. 1062 of 2008 and obtained the Rule in which further proceeding has been stayed. 

 9. Mr. Khurshid Alam Khan, the learned Advocate for the accused petitioner submits that in order to make a person liable under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act  the payee of a cheques has to give a notice in writing to the drawer of the cheques within 15 days of the receipt of information by him from the Bank regarding the return of the cheques as unpaid in terms of clause ( B) to the provision; that the drawer of the cheques is obliged to make the payment within 15 days of the receipt of the said notice failing which the cause of action for prosecution will arise under clause(C) and that here in the instant case non-disclosure of the concerned Bank, the cause of action for prosecution has not been arisen and as such the impugned proceedings is an abuse of the process of the court which is liable to be quashed for securing ends of justice in this case. 

 10. Mr. Sheikh Azmol Hayet, the learned Advocate for the opposite party No. 2, on the other hand, submits that mere omission to mention the name of the Bank cannot frustrate the proceeding and that the whole allegation as brought in the petition of complaint requires to be adjudicated on production of oral and documentary evidence to be produced by the complainant at the time of trial. He further submits that in the instant case, cheques were lastly dishonoured on 18.05.2006; that notice was issued on 23.05.2006 and the petition of complaint was filed on 25.06.2006. In view of the facts, it is apparent that there is no violation of section 138 and 141 of the Negotiable Instruments Act in initiation of the proceeding. The learned Advocate for the opposite party No. 2 by filing a counter affidavit stated that accused issued 3 cheques bearing Nos. 3423147, 3423148 and 3423152 dated 28.11.2005, 29.11.2005 and 29.11.2005 respectively from his current account No. 71001429 of United Commercial Bank Ltd. Agrabad Branch, Chittagong in favour of the complainant and that the application purports the disputed question of facts which cannot be decided in the miscellaneous jurisdiction under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and in the circumstances of the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 11. In order to appreciate the submission made by the learned Advocates for the accused petitioner and the opposite party No.2, let us now see whether the complainant opposite party No. 2 has filed the case before the learned Magistrate strictly complying with the provision of law envisaged under section 138 and 141 of the Negotiable Instruments Act and whether the proceedings under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure is liable to be quashed. Now let us see the provision of section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments act which reads as follows: 

 (b) The payee or the holder in due course of the cheque, as the case may be, makes a demand for the payment of the said amount of money by giving a notice, in writing, to the drawer of the cheque, within thirty days of the receipt of information by him from the bank regarding the return of the cheque as unpaid, and 

 (c) The drawer of such cheque fails to make the payment of the said amount of money to the payee or, as the case may be, to the holder in due course of the cheque, within (thirty days) of the receipt of the said notice. 

 (a) No court shall take cognizance of any offence punishable under section 138 except upon a complaint, in writing, made by the payee or, as the case may be, the holder in due course of the cheque; 

 16. Now the point for determination is (1) whether the petitioner filed the case satisfying the provisions of law and (II) whether taking cognizance of the offence in this case is in contravention of law and (III) whether the continuation of the case is legal. 

 18. The only point of dispute is whether the complainant has filed the case as per the provision of law 

 19. On perusal of the record it appears that the notice for demand of money was issued on 23.05.2006 There is nothing in the complaint when the said notice was actually served on the accused petitioner. The case of the opposite party No.2 is that the legal notice under section 138 (1) (b) of the Negotiable Instrument act was issued on 23.05.2006 through registered post with AD; that it is presumed as per the provision of law that the said notice has been duly served upon the accused petitioner but the accused petitioner did not turn up to clear up the dues after getting notice as per the provision of law. 

 20. The only contention of the accused petitioner is that there is no mentioning of the date of service of notice and thus no cause of action arose for the instant case and as such the proceedings of the instant case is liable to be quashed. 

 21. Since the notice was issued through registered post with AD and its receipt has been marked as annexure-1 and thus it is deemed to be served on and received by the accused petitioner, so it can be legally presumed that the notice has been served properly as per article 17 of General Clauses Act. The accused petitioner nowhere in his entire petition mentioned that he did not receive the legal notice. There is nothing in the four corners of section 138 or of section 141 of the Negotiable Instruments Act that for non-mentioning of receiving date of the legal notice in the petition of complaint, the case will render illegal when all other ingredients in filling the case is very much available in the materials on record. We find support of the case above view in the case of Nizamuddin Mahmood vs. Abdul Hamid Bhuiyan and another reported in 60 DLR (AD) 195. 

 22. More so the very correctness of serving legal notice under sectionl 38(1)(B) of the act by the payee Bank and receiving so by the drawer or the cheque can only be adjudicated in the trial and as such the proceeding cannot be quashed for factual aspect of a case. Whatever the defence case might be, that cannot be the basis of quashing the proceedings initiated against the petitioner when it proves that the alleged cheque has been issued by him and it was bounced from his bank. 

 23. In this connection we may profitably refers the decision in the case of Nizamuddin Mahmood vs. Abdul Hamid Bhuiyan and another reported in 60 DLR (AD) 195 wherein their Lordships held " Since the date of receipt is a question of fact to be ascertained at the time of trial non-disclosure of such fact in the complaint petition cannot render the proceeding liable to be quashed to the great prejudice of the complainant who is entitled to prove his case on evidence." 

 25. The next question for determination as to whether the filing of the case is pre-mature or not. 

 26. It appears that the legal notice was issued on 25.11.2007 and the case was filed on 23.12.2007 i.e. the case was filed after 28 days of the issuance of legal notice. Apparently it appears that the case filed before maturity. In this connection we profitable refer the decsion Satya Narayan Podder vs. State reported in 53 DLR wherein their lordship decided "even though the case is pre-mature and it was filed before the expiry of 15 days from the date of receipt of the notice, the proceedings is not liable to be quashed." 

 27. We have considered the decision of our Appellate Division on such a question of pre-maturity of cause of action. This is reported in 31 DLR (AD) 118. This decision is relating to the pre-maturity of cause of action regarding to the pre-emption case. The principle laid down in this case is that if the cause of action is matured during the pendency of the proceedings, the defect of pre-maturity of cause of action could be cured. Though the above principle is laid down in respect of the Civil Proceeding, we are of the view that the spirit of this principle can be applied even in a Criminal case. 

 28. In the instant case, in the light of the decisions referred hereinbefore we could safely presume that though the instant case was filed before prematurity which will not help the petitioner and as such the complaint is not time barred. 

 29. In this connection we may also profitably refer the decision in the case of Ali Akkas vs. Enayet Hossain and others reported in 17 BLD (AD) 44 wherein their Lordships held: "the settled principle of law is that to bring a case within the purview of section 561A for the purpose of quashing a proceeding one of following conditions must be fulfilled: 

 (1) Interference even at an initial stage may be justified where the facts are so preposterous that even on admitted facts no case stands against the accused; 

 (4) In a case where the allegations in the FIR or the petition of complaint, even if taken at their face value and accepted in their entirely, do not constitute the offence alleged; and 

 (5) The allegations against the accused although constituted an offence alleged but there is either no legal evidence adduced in support of the case or the evidence adduced clearly or manifestly fails to prove the charge." 

 30. In the light of the above decision and considering the facts and circumstances of the case, we are of the view that since there is no legal bar against the initiation and continuation of the proceedings and as such the proceedings does not amount to an abuse of the process of the court we could safely presumed that the proceedings shall not be quashed and the accused petitioner is not therefore entitled to get relief as prayed for and as such the Rule should be discharged. 

 31. In the result the Rule is discharged and the proceedings of sessions case No. 1062 of 2006 arising out of CR Case No. 183 of 2006 (Doublemooring Zone) under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act which is now pending in the court of learned Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge, 1st Court, Chittagong should not be quashed. The Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge, 1st Court, Chittagong is directed to dispose of the case within 6(six) months from the date of receipt of this order.
